$comment: Scripts removed during the plan-13 duplicate-command cleanup (2026-07-04). Kept for reference — these commands worked but were redundant (identical to another script, or referenced a task name nothing invokes). If you need any of them back, copy the entry into the corresponding package.json `scripts` block. Each entry is keyed by package path.

dev:apps.reason: Identical to `dev`. Removed; `dev` does the same thing.

redis:down.reason: Identical to `services:down`. The name implied it stopped only redis, but `docker compose down` stops ALL services. Removed as misleading; use `services:down`.

redis:logs.reason: Narrow per-service log tail. Removed in favor of the single `services:logs` (`docker compose logs -f`) which you can Ctrl-C / filter. To follow one service: `docker compose logs -f redis`.

db:down.reason: Identical to `services:down`. Same misleading-name issue as `redis:down`. Removed; use `services:down`.

db:logs.reason: Narrow per-service log tail. Removed in favor of `services:logs`. To follow one service: `docker compose logs -f postgres`.

build:dev.reason: Identical to `build`. Removed; `build` is the dev build (APP_ENV=development). `build:prod` is kept (APP_ENV=production).
Identical to `build`. Removed; `build` is the canonical command.

# Development commands.reason: Empty-string 'comment' script (npm shows it in `npm run` output but it does nothing). Removed; comments belong in this archive file or in README.

# Production commands.reason: Empty-string 'comment' script. Removed; same as above.

$notes.build:prod: KEPT in every package — it's a real, used distinction (root `npm run build:prod` → `turbo run build:prod`; web's build:prod sets APP_ENV=production).
$notes.build:dev turbo task: Also removed from every turbo.json (root + apps + packages) since no script defines it anymore. `turbo run build` covers the dev build.
$notes.dev: KEPT (the primary dev command). `dev:all` KEPT (includes package watchers).
$notes.service-scoped docker: For one-service operations, call docker compose directly: `docker compose up -d redis`, `docker compose logs -f postgres`. The `services:*` aggregate scripts remain.
